The '''2021–22 Scottish Premiership''' (known as the '''[[Cinch (company)|cinch]] Premiership''' for sponsorship reasons) was the ninth season of the [[Scottish Premiership]], the highest division of [[Football in Scotland|Scottish football]], and the 125th edition overall of the top national league competition, not including one cancelled due to [[World War II]]. The season began on 31 July 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/start-dates-for-202122|title=Start dates for 2021/22|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=25 March 2021}}</ref> In December, the Scottish Government imposed stadium capacity restrictions as part of its response to the new [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant|Omicron variant]]. As a result, the winter break was brought forward from 4 January to 27 December.<ref>{{cite news|title=Premiership winter break brought forward|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59760055|date=22 December 2021|access-date=13 January 2022}}</ref> The rule of five substitutions per match was also re-introduced (as used the previous season) after the winter break.<ref>{{cite news|title=Premiership clubs allowed five subs|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59980853|date=13 January 2022|access-date=13 January 2022}}</ref>

Twelve teams contested the league: [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]], [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] and [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

On 11 May 2022, Celtic officially claimed the Premiership title back from Rangers following a 1–1 draw with Dundee United, going undefeated in the final 32 league matches of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dundee United 1–1 Celtic: Ange Postecoglou's side reclaim league title|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61316038|date=11 May 2022|access-date=11 May 2022}}</ref>

| {{flagicon|SCO}} [[David Gray (footballer, born 1988)|David Gray]] (caretaker)
| 19 April 2022<ref name="Maloney"/>

==Format==
In the initial phase of the season, the 12 teams will play a round-robin tournament whereby each team plays each one of the other teams three times. After 33 games, the league splits into two sections of six teams, with each team playing each other in that section. The league attempts to balance the fixture list so that teams in the same section play each other twice at home and twice away, but sometimes this is impossible. A total of 228 matches will be played, with 38 matches played by each team.

==Premiership play-offs==
The quarter-finals were contested by the teams placed third and fourth in the [[2021–22 Scottish Championship#League summary|2021–22 Scottish Championship]]. The winners advanced to the semi-finals to face the team placed second in the Championship. The final was contested by the semi-final winners and the team placed eleventh in the Premiership, with the winners securing a place in the [[2022–23 Scottish Premiership]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/spfl-press-release-48366|title=Press Release: Play-offs &#124; SPFL|website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref>

==Broadcasting==
=== Live matches (UK and Ireland) ===
Sky Sports had exclusive rights to the Scottish Premiership, showing up to 48 matches and the Premiership play-off final.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46264665 |title=Scottish Premiership: Matches to be shown live on Sky only as new £160m TV deal struck |first=Chris |last=McLaughlin |date=19 November 2018 |access-date=25 February 2020 |publisher=BBC |website=BBC Sport |archive-date=28 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200128072708/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46264665 |url-status=live }}</ref> BBC Scotland broadcast the Premiership quarter-final and semi-final play-off ties.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/play-off-games-on-bbc | title=SPFL play-offs on BBC Scotland | publisher=Scottish Professional Football League | date=5 May 2021 | access-date=16 May 2021}}</ref>

Due to the impact of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], clubs continued to stream matches (not broadcast on Sky) to fans on a pay-per-view or "virtual season ticket" basis, whilst capacities in stadia were limited due to social distancing restrictions.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/press-release-47629 | title=Press Release | publisher=Scottish Professional Football League | date=19 April 2021 | access-date=16 May 2021}}</ref>

=== Highlights ===
Highlights were broadcast on [[BBC Scotland]]'s flagship [[Sportscene]] programme on both Saturdays and Sundays. Sky Sports also showed highlights.

Gaelic-language channel [[BBC Alba]] had rights to broadcast repeats in full of 38 Saturday 15:00 matches "as live" at 17:30. 

The SPFL also uploaded the goals from every Premiership match onto its [[YouTube]] channel.
